findings.problem: Two theorems finish with the same five-step transfer argument. After `apply AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.mapMulEquiv.injective` there are `hcomp` (`apply_symm_apply` of the composite), `hp` (`apply_symm_apply` of the base point), `hpcomp` (`congrArg` of the composition operator applied to `hp.symm`) and `hnat` (the Hopf-algebra naturality lemma, reversed). The proof ends with `exact hcomp.trans (hpcomp.trans hnat)`. The argument is: an equivalence `e` semiconjugates `F` to a postcomposition or precomposition `T` on the target side, so `e.symm (T q) = F (e.symm q)`. It is proved twice by hand, with long expressions copied into each block. The first use is at lines 210–224 (T is precomposition by `Spec.map phi`). The second is at lines 277–290 (T is postcomposition by `hopfSpecMapAsOver f`). A third naturality statement would need the same 15 lines again.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one private lemma:
`private lemma symm_apply_of_semiconj {α β : Type*} (e : α ≃ β) (F : α → α) (T : β → β) (h : ∀ x, e (F x) = T (e x)) (q : β) : e.symm (T q) = F (e.symm q)`.
Proof: `apply e.injective; rw [e.apply_symm_apply, h, e.apply_symm_apply]`.

Use 1 (`groupSchemePointsMulEquiv_mapValue`): keep the `change` and `rw [Category.assoc]`. Then close with `exact symm_apply_of_semiconj AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.mapMulEquiv.toEquiv (HopfAlgebra.mapPoints (H := (coordinateRing R G).obj) (CommAlgCat.ofHom phi)) (fun q => (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom phi.toRingHom)).asOver (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) ≫ q) (fun x => CommHopfAlgCat.mapMulEquiv_mapValue (coordinateRing R G).obj (CommAlgCat.ofHom phi) x) (p ≫ (groupSchemeIsoSpec (R := R) G).hom)`.

Use 2 (`groupSchemePointsMulEquiv_groupSchemeMap`): keep the `change` and the `rw [Category.assoc, groupSchemeIsoSpec_naturality, ← Category.assoc]`. Then close with the same lemma, taking `F := (CommHopfAlgCat.Hom.mapPointsFunctor (coordinateMap R f).hom).app (CommAlgCat.of R A)`, `T := fun q => q ≫ hopfSpecMapAsOver (R := R) f`, `h := fun x => CommHopfAlgCat.mapMulEquiv_mapDomain (CommAlgCat.of R A) (coordinateMap R f).hom.hom x`, and `q := p ≫ (groupSchemeIsoSpec (R := R) H).hom`.

The hypotheses and imports are unchanged. The lemma needs only `Equiv` and sits in this file.
findings.benefit: The `hcomp`/`hp`/`hpcomp`/`hnat` pattern, with its long repeated `p ≫ (groupSchemeIsoSpec …).hom` expressions, is stated and proved once. Each theorem is then reduced to its distinguishing data: the semiconjugacy lemma and the choice of `F` and `T`. This makes the mathematical content (naturality of the Spec equivalence) visible. It removes about 25 lines and gives future naturality statements, such as other functors on points, a ready tool.
